---
title: "Cross-Country Transfer Learning for ICU Admission Prediction"
---

::: {.project-meta}
In progress · Manuscript in preparation · Feb 2026 – present · Statistical Learning Across Biomedicine (S-LAB), Jeonbuk National University
:::

Predicting whether a patient will require admission to an intensive care unit,
using electronic health record data from several countries. The central question
is how far a model trained on one country's records transfers to another, and how
much data from the target country is needed to close the gap that remains.

## Data

Multi-country electronic health records.
PLACEHOLDER: name the source databases, countries, cohort sizes, and the outcome
definition used for ICU admission.

## Methods

TabPFN, a prior-fitted transformer for tabular data, as the primary predictive
model, evaluated against PLACEHOLDER: baseline comparators. Training in a source
country with evaluation in held-out target countries, followed by target
adaptation using PLACEHOLDER: adaptation strategy. Sensitivity of the reported
gains to label noise is assessed separately, and results are checked for
reproducibility across repeated splits and random seeds.
